comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
MEASUREMENT REFINED — the silent class is ~5 assertions, not 255, and a GREEN SUITE IS EVIDENCE OF THE
BUG rather than evidence against it.

## The 255 figure was the wrong denominator

Splitting the 255 `caplog` occurrences by what they do when zero records arrive:

    NEGATIVE assertions — PASS VACUOUSLY when void (the severe class):        5
      tests/unit/test_agent_build_invariants.py:147  assert not any("zeroed/implausible" in r.message ...)
      tests/unit/test_usage_log.py:254               assert not caplog.records
      tests/unit/test_config_default_assignee.py:75  assert not any("default_assignee" in r.message ...)
      tests/unit/test_config_llm.py:197              assert not any("llm" in r.getMessage().lower() ...)
      (plus one further match)

    POSITIVE assertions — FAIL LOUDLY when void:                             25
      `assert any(... caplog ...)` raises AssertionError; `next(... caplog ...)` raises StopIteration.

The remaining occurrences are setup, `caplog.at_level(...)` and similar, not assertions.

So the coverage-integrity problem — an assertion that verifies nothing while reporting success — is
about FIVE assertions. The other 25 are a FLAKINESS problem: they announce themselves by going red, as
one of them did. Auditing all 255 would waste the effort; auditing these 5 is a bounded job. This
supersedes the "54 files / 255 occurrences" search space in the description above.

## A GREEN SUITE DOES NOT MEAN THE POISONING DIDN'T HAPPEN

A full default-selection run on CLEAN main at 6cdd4b00d passed: 9219 passed, exit 0. That is NOT
evidence the mechanism is absent — the mechanism was proven directly on that same clean tree
(`configure_logging()` flips `logging.getLogger("rebar").propagate` True -> False and never restores
it).

The two observations are consistent, and the reason is the whole point of this ticket: if the
poisoning occurred in that run, the five negative assertions would have PASSED VACUOUSLY and the run
would still be green. The only reason anyone noticed at all is that ONE victim happened to use
`next(...)`, which raises on an empty iterator instead of quietly succeeding.

That is the sharpest available statement of the defect: WE CANNOT TELL, FROM A GREEN RUN, WHETHER THOSE
FIVE ASSERTIONS VERIFIED ANYTHING. Determining it requires instrumentation, not inspection of the
result.

## Consequence for the acceptance criteria

The first AC (establish how many assertions are currently void) should be scoped to these five and
answered by INSTRUMENTATION — e.g. record, per test, whether `logging.getLogger("rebar").propagate` was
True at assertion time and whether any records were captured. Counting from a green run cannot answer
it, because green is exactly what a void assertion produces.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
GUARD LANDED in commit 2f2a981c61 (not pushed). Plus the measurement AC1 asked for, and a
SECOND poisoner that is live today.

## AC1 ANSWERED BY INSTRUMENTATION: 0 of the 5 negative assertions are void

A temporary pytest plugin recorded, per test, `logging.getLogger("rebar").propagate` and the
captured-record count at the end of the call phase, over a full default-selection run
(`-n 6 --dist worksteal`). All five targets were reached and ALL FIVE had propagate=True:

  tests/unit/test_agent_build_invariants.py::test_usage_plausibility_silent_on_normal
  tests/unit/test_usage_log.py::test_summarize_marks_unknown_model_unpriced
  tests/unit/test_config_default_assignee.py::test_key_is_known_no_unknown_warning
  tests/unit/test_config_llm.py::test_core_load_config_does_not_warn_on_llm_table
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_check_canonical_heldout.py::test_no_spurious_truncation_warning

The plugin also emitted a row for ANY test observed with propagate=False. There were none.

Liveness confirmed positively, not just by absence: injecting the exact record each assertion
forbids (matching logger + token) makes ALL FIVE go red - `5 failed in 0.82s`. So none is a
green no-op; nothing had to be restored or deleted under AC4.

Why they are immune to the level vector below: each uses `caplog.at_level(WARNING, logger=...)`
or asserts at WARNING, and a logger level only gates at the ORIGINATING logger, so a raised
`rebar` level does not reach them. The victims of the level vector are INFO-level assertions.

## WHY THE PROPAGATE VECTOR FOUND NOTHING - pytest already half-mitigates it

`_pytest.logging.catching_logs.__enter__` (pytest 9.1.1) attaches the capture handler to every
logger that is ALREADY non-propagating. Its own comment names the hole: "will miss loggers that
*become* non-propagating after the `__enter__`". So the void window is one test PHASE wide, not
process-wide. The description premise that one call voids everything downstream does not hold on
this pytest; the ticket comment 2 prediction that the 5 would show as vacuous is therefore not
what the instrumentation found. The window is still silent, and relying on a _pytest internal is
not a control, so the guard still earns its place.

## SECOND POISONER, PROVEN, AND IT IS THE LIVE ONE: the LEVEL, not propagation

`rebar._logging.install_stderr_handler()` does `logger.setLevel(WARNING)` on the shared `rebar`
logger, process-global, never restored. `rebar._cli.main()` calls it on EVERY invocation, and 11
test files call `main()` in-process. After that, an INFO record on any `rebar.*` logger is dropped
AT THE ORIGINATING LOGGER, and `caplog.at_level(logging.INFO)` with no `logger=` argument CANNOT
rescue it because it raises the ROOT level only.

Three-test probe, clean tree - identical assertion either side of a `main(["--help"])` call:
`test_a_baseline` PASSES, `test_b_poison_via_cli_main` prints `AFTER level: 30`,
`test_c_same_assertion_after` FAILS. This is the reported b718 symptom exactly, and unlike the
propagate vector it fires in every default run.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION OF THE REPORTED FLAKE, in-repo, one process:
  pytest -p no:randomly tests/unit/test_llm_setup_cli.py tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py
  with the guard      -> 17 passed
  guard mutated off   -> 1 failed: test_success_telemetry_survives_an_empty_usage_dict
                         - StopIteration at test_agent_call_seam.py:159
Byte-identical to the originally reported failure. The intermittency was never mysterious: it was
whether worksteal put a CLI-invoking test on the same worker before this one. The guard both makes
it deterministic and fixes it.

## THE GUARD, AND WHY THE TWO VECTORS ARE TREATED DIFFERENTLY

Autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py, detection in tests/_log_integrity.py (same split as the
repo-isolation guard, so the self-test drives the same code, not a copy):

  * propagate=False -> FAIL the test, named at the SOURCE ("<nodeid> disabled it during its own
    body"), and restore propagation so no downstream victim is blamed instead. A separate
    setup-phase message covers an out-of-band (import/collection-time) kill and explicitly does
    NOT accuse the test it lands on.
  * level raised -> CONTAIN: snapshot at setup, restore at teardown, no blame. Raising it is a
    legitimate side effect of exercising a real entrypoint in-process. Containment is strictly
    stronger than blame here for coverage integrity - every test then starts from the same level,
    so its log assertions hold regardless of run order - whereas failing would force ~11 files to
    add cleanup for no additional safety.

## MUTATION EVIDENCE BOTH DIRECTIONS (permanent, in the self-test)

tests/unit/test_caplog_coverage_integrity.py, 11 tests, via pytester so the same poisoned file is
run with and without the guard - the guard is the only difference:

  propagate vector: unguarded -> 1 passed, ret 0 (the fail-open reproduced: a vacuous assertion
                    reports success); guarded -> 1 passed + 1 error, ret != 0, and the output
                    names test_kills_propagation_mid_capture as the source.
  level vector:     unguarded -> a later INFO assertion FAILS; guarded -> 2 passed.
  no cascade:       the test after the poisoner sees propagate=True and captures normally.
  clean run:        unaffected, ret 0.

## COORDINATION WITH b718 - no duplicated mechanism

b718 (commit 590e0e070f) is a PRODUCTION-code fix: configure_logging() stops mutating propagate.
9ac2 is a TEST-HARNESS guard covering the class. Neither reimplements the other: b718 removes one
source, the guard catches any future source plus the level vector b718 does not touch. b718 must
land first, or the guard fails test_configure_logging_emits_rebar_info_to_stdout at teardown -
which is itself the guard demonstrating it catches the source.

Gates by exit code: make lint 0, make typecheck 0. Not pushed to Gerrit; ticket left in_progress.

comments.body:
GATE STATUS at handoff. make lint exit 0, make typecheck exit 0 (mypy, 416 files). Consolidated
regression over the affected set - test_review_bot, test_caplog_coverage_integrity,
test_agent_call_seam, test_llm_setup_cli, test_repo_isolation_guard, and all four remaining
negative-assertion files - 168 passed, 6 skipped, exit 0, from a verified-clean worktree
(git status --porcelain empty immediately before the run and again after).

The FULL default selection did NOT complete. Not a failure: this host is saturated by other
agents (load average peaked at 66 with three other full suites running) and the run advanced
about 1% per 10 minutes. Two earlier attempts were killed by the harness at ~50 min with exit
144 - a kill, not a test result. The third is running DETACHED (nohup, pid 57403) and was at 26%
at handoff, writing to /tmp/final_run2.txt; tail that file for the verdict.

Nothing in the change set is plausibly order-sensitive in a way the targeted runs miss - the
guard makes ordering LESS load-bearing, not more - but the full-selection exit code is still
owed before either ticket closes.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

A `caplog` assertion whose records never arrive DOES NOT FAIL — it passes vacuously. `assert not
[unexpected]` is trivially true against an empty list, and even a positive `assert any(...)` only fails
if someone wrote it that way. So a test can lose 100% of its coverage and stay GREEN, permanently and
silently, with nothing in the run output distinguishing it from a test that genuinely verified
something.

This is not hypothetical. It is happening in this repository right now.

## The live instance

`src/rebar/review_bot/config.py:145-146` (`configure_logging()`) sets

    lg = logging.getLogger("rebar")
    lg.propagate = False

process-globally, and never restores it. pytest's `caplog` captures through a handler on the ROOT
logger, so once propagation is off NO `rebar.*` record can reach it again for the remainder of the
process. Every later `caplog` assertion on a rebar logger silently sees zero records.

Proven on a clean tree by a two-test probe: identical assertion, passes before `configure_logging()`
and fails after; `caplog.at_level()` does not help because it adjusts LEVELS, not propagation. Full
mechanism, both entry points, and the reproduction are on ticket b718-fb7f-b1a4-4feb — including that
`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:202` calls `configure_logging()` at MODULE IMPORT time, so merely
importing the app poisons the process (inert in this checkout only because `fastapi` is absent).

b718 fixes THE POISONER. This ticket is about the far larger problem it exposed: THE SUITE CANNOT TELL
THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A PASSING ASSERTION AND AN UNREACHABLE ONE.

## Blast radius — measured, though the precise void count is unknown

    54 test files contain `caplog`
    255 total `caplog` occurrences

How many of those are currently void in a full run is NOT established, and establishing it is the
first job of this ticket. The count depends on run order and on which logger each assertion targets,
and `-n 6 --dist worksteal` distributes tests across workers nondeterministically — so the SAME
assertion may be live in one run and void in the next, on the same commit. That non-determinism is
itself part of the defect: coverage is not reproducible.

## Why this is severe rather than untidy

* IT FAILS OPEN. Every other gate in this repo fails closed. This one silently reports success.
* IT IS INVISIBLE. Nothing in the output marks a void assertion. Reviewers, CI and agents all see
  green.
* IT SURVIVED DETECTION. It was found only as a side effect of debugging an unrelated ticket, by an
  agent that noticed one victim test and traced it. Nobody was looking for it.
* IT IS ORDER-DEPENDENT, so a test can be genuinely verifying in isolation — which is how it was
  written and reviewed — and verify nothing in the suite that actually gates merges.
* THE VICTIM IS NEVER THE CULPRIT. The one test that DID go red pointed at
  `test_agent_call_seam.py`, nowhere near `review_bot/config.py`.

## Approach

Fixing the current poisoner (b718) removes today's instance but not the class — any future code that
touches logger propagation, handlers or levels reintroduces it, with the same silence.

The durable fix is to make an unreachable log assertion FAIL LOUDLY instead of passing. Candidates to
weigh, not yet decided:
  * an autouse fixture that asserts `logging.getLogger("rebar").propagate` is True at test setup, so
    the poisoning is caught at the point of damage rather than at a random later victim;
  * a `caplog` wrapper/fixture used by rebar tests that fails when zero records were captured for an
    assertion that expected some;
  * making `configure_logging()` scoped/restorable so no test can leak it in the first place (overlaps
    b718 — coordinate rather than duplicate).
The first is the smallest change that converts a silent fail-open into a loud fail-closed, and it
protects against future reintroduction rather than just this instance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The number of `caplog` assertions currently void in a full default-selection run is ESTABLISHED
      and recorded — not estimated. The 54-file / 255-occurrence figures above are the search space,
      not the answer.
- [ ] An unreachable log assertion FAILS rather than passing vacuously, and a test proves it: with
      propagation deliberately disabled, a previously-green assertion must go RED.
- [ ] The guard catches the poisoning AT ITS SOURCE, not at a random later victim — a test asserts the
      failure names the code that disabled propagation, not an unrelated downstream test.
- [ ] Any assertion found to be void is either restored to working coverage or deleted; none is left
      passing vacuously. Deleting is acceptable where the assertion no longer earns its place, but
      leaving a green no-op is not.
- [ ] Coordinated with b718 so the poisoner fix and the class guard do not implement overlapping
      mechanisms.
- [ ] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
compiled_state.title: Unreachable caplog assertions pass vacuously: the suite cannot distinguish verified coverage from zero coverage
